events.summary: Scoped to: a new Makefile release-bundle target plus hack/make-deterministic-tarball.py and hack/BUNDLE-README.md.tmpl it uses; an additive hack/verify-release.py --bundle mode plus hack/test_verify_release.py and hack/test_make_deterministic_tarball.py tests; ONE new appended job (release-bundle) in .github/workflows/release.yaml, added after release-manifest with no existing job reordered or edited; a README 'Air-gapped installation' section. Explicitly out of scope and untouched: charts/** templates, internal/**, Dockerfile, ci.yaml, release-manifest.json's schemaVersion (stays 3 -- see e1), and the upgrade/rollback/zero-egress-smoke-test gaps the issue also names, which are separate, sequential lanes

Defect framed honestly: before this change, no release artifact could be installed on a cluster with zero outbound network access -- the multi-arch image was only ever pushed to GHCR (a pull is itself network egress), and hack/verify-release.py could verify a downloaded release directory's binaries/chart/sbom/signatures but had no way to verify an offline bundle at all, since none existed. Fix, in three pieces: (1) `make release-bundle` (Makefile) packages an already-built image reference (IMAGE_REF, exported to an OCI archive via `docker save` + `skopeo copy docker-archive:...` when the image is already loaded locally, else `skopeo copy docker://...` for a pushed ref, else `docker buildx --output type=oci` as a last resort) and an already-packaged chart .tgz (CHART_TGZ) into one deterministic tarball. (2) hack/make-deterministic-tarball.py builds that tarball via Python's stdlib tarfile instead of shelling out to the platform `tar`, because GNU tar's --sort/--mtime/--owner flags either don't exist or behave differently on macOS's bundled bsdtar -- discovered directly by testing: a first implementation using `tar --sort=name --mtime=... --owner=0` in the Makefile produced different digests on two runs on this (macOS/bsdtar) host, so the whole file-writing step was moved into Python instead, sorting the member list by relpath and zeroing mtime/uid/gid/uname/gname on every entry. (3) hack/verify-release.py's new --bundle mode checks: the bundle's own sha256 (against release-manifest.json's optional 'bundle' field if present, else a sidecar <bundle>.sha256 file -- deliberately NOT a new manifest field, since release-manifest.json is already signed by the time this bundle exists, and retrofitting a field into it would invalidate that signature -- see e1), the OCI archive's image digest (read from its index.json) against the manifest's image.digest, and the chart .tgz inside the bundle against the manifest's chart.sha256.

Before fixing the tarball-writer, `tar --sort=name --mtime=@$SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH --owner=0 --group=0 --numeric-owner -czf bundle.tar.gz -C stage .` run twice over byte-identical staged input on this macOS host (bsdtar 3.5.3/libarchive) produced two different sha256 digests -- bsdtar doesn't support --sort/--owner/--numeric-owner the way GNU tar does, so member order and ownership metadata leaked through non-deterministically. Separately, after switching to the Python tarfile-based writer, a second reproducibility bug surfaced in testing: two runs writing to *different output filenames* (out1.tar.gz vs out2.tar.gz) over identical content still produced different sha256 digests, traced to gzip.GzipFile defaulting to the output file's own .name attribute as the embedded FNAME header field when no explicit filename is passed -- fixed by passing filename="" explicitly. Both defects were caught by tests (a Makefile-level double-build for the first, hack/test_make_deterministic_tarball.py's test_two_runs_over_identical_input_are_byte_identical for the second) before being treated as fixed.

events.summary: Part of #5 is advanced: an offline/air-gap install bundle now exists (make release-bundle, wired into release.yaml as one appended job), is reproducible byte-for-byte across repeated local builds, and has an additive, tested offline verifier (hack/verify-release.py --bundle) plus a README section and a BUNDLE-README.md walkthrough shipped inside every bundle. release-manifest.json's schemaVersion intentionally stayed at 3 per the issue's own review-pass guidance (e1). Not addressed by this PR and left for separate, sequential lanes per the issue's own gap list: an actual zero-egress CI smoke test that installs from the bundle, cosign verification of the container image itself (as opposed to blob signatures), and helm upgrade/rollback automation

Complete for the scope in e2 (offline bundle build tooling, CI wiring, additive verifier mode, docs), verified at the level in e5. Unverified: the release.yaml job's actual CI run (only a tagged push triggers it), multi-arch bundle contents, and registry-pull path of the image export
